scenes.title: TRUNCATE TABLE
scenes.narration: TRUNCATE TABLE quickly empties a table of all rows while keeping its structure intact.

scenes.title: Emptying a table
bullets: Faster than deleting rows one by one
scenes.narration: TRUNCATE TABLE clears out all rows from a table in a single operation. The table's structure, including columns and constraints, stays fully in place. Because it does not log each row removal individually, it is far faster than a broad DELETE.

scenes.title: Emptying a staging table
scenes.narration: This statement wipes every row from the staging_events table. The table itself remains, ready to receive a fresh batch of data. It is a common step before reloading a staging area in a pipeline.

scenes.heading: TRUNCATE vs DELETE
scenes.narration: TRUNCATE removes every row quickly but offers no way to filter which rows go. DELETE is more precise, letting a WHERE clause target specific rows. That flexibility comes at the cost of speed on large tables.

scenes.text: Reach for TRUNCATE to reset an entire table fast, and DELETE when you need row-level control.
scenes.narration: Use TRUNCATE for a fast full reset of a table, and switch to DELETE whenever you need to remove only some of the rows.
